core_obligations: Set up the criterion (proof lines 9484-9487): condition (1) of the total acyclicity criterion holds by the preliminary lemma on the pullback of an injective module, so it remains to check the exactness of the alternating complex of sections over the fibre products.

Use the commutativity with fibre products (proof lines 9488-9498): for a surjective map K' -> K of sheaves of sets the induced map g_!^{Sh}K' -> g_!^{Sh}K is surjective because the lower shriek is a left adjoint, and the assumption that it commutes with fibre products identifies the sections of the pullback over the n-fold fibre product with the sections of I over the n-fold fibre product of the images, giving the displayed chain of equalities.

Conclude total acyclicity (proof lines 9499-9507): an injective module is totally acyclic by the cited lemma applied to the identity, so the converse of the criterion yields the exactness of the complex 0 -> H^0(K, g^{-1}I) -> H^0(K', g^{-1}I) -> H^0(K' x_K K', g^{-1}I) -> ..., which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Check condition (1) of the total acyclicity criterion by the preliminary vanishing lemma.
Rewrite the sections of the pullback over fibre products using the commutativity with fibre products of the lower shriek.
Apply the total acyclicity of injective modules and the converse of the criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a continuous and cocontinuous functor of sites whose lower shriek on sheaves of sets commutes with fibre products, the pullback of an injective module along the associated morphism of topoi is totally acyclic (statement lines 9470-9482). The proof (proof lines 9484-9508) checks condition (1) of the total acyclicity criterion, computes the sections over fibre products through the commutativity hypothesis, and concludes with the total acyclicity of injective modules and the converse of the criterion. H2: two independent inputs and one computation, written out in full.
